models_evaluated: commercially available deep learning-based detection algorithm (DLD) detecting nine chest radiograph findings

links.outcome: Sensitivity when the AI-ranked lower 50% of radiographs were treated as negative without radiologist review versus reading all
links.effect: Sensitivity was 82.6% reading all without DLD and 83.5% in the 50% worklist reduction scenario; difference 0.8% (95% CI -3.8% to 5.5%), noninferior. Specificity rose from 86.7% to 90.4%.
links.quote: The difference in sensitivity was 0.8% (95% CI: - 3.8%, 5.5%), establishing noninferiority of 50% worklist reduction (p = 0.01).

models_evaluated: commercially available deep learning-based detection algorithm (DLD)

links.outcome: sensitivity and specificity after DLD triage
links.effect: Sensitivity was 83.5% (197 of 236) with 50% reduction vs 82.6% (195 of 236) without DLD; specificity increased 86.7% to 90.4% (p < 0.001).
links.quote: The sensitivity was 82.6% (195 of 236; 95% CI: 77.5%, 87.3%) when readers interpreted all chest radiographs without DLD and 83.5% (197 of 236; 95% CI: 78.8%, 88.1%) in the 50% worklist reduction scenario.

links.effect: Difference in sensitivity was 0.8% (95% CI: - 3.8%, 5.5%), establishing noninferiority of 50% worklist reduction (p = 0.01).
links.quote: The difference in sensitivity was 0.8% (95% CI: - 3.8%, 5.5%), establishing noninferiority of 50% worklist reduction (p = 0.01).

links.outcome: sensitivity and specificity under worklist reduction
links.effect: Sensitivity was noninferior (83.5% vs 82.6%, difference 0.8%, p=0.01) and specificity was higher (90.4% vs 86.7%, p<0.001) with 50% worklist reduction compared to reading all radiographs without AI.
links.quote: The sensitivity was 82.6% (195 of 236; 95% CI: 77.5%, 87.3%) when readers interpreted all chest radiographs without DLD and 83.5% (197 of 236; 95% CI: 78.8%, 88.1%) in the 50% worklist reduction scenario.
